item.title: Mini Crackme: Bitwise NOT Check
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64, fastcall (first int arg in ecx).
A "license check" function takes one byte (a character) in cl and returns 1 (pass) or 0 (fail). Find the single-character input that makes it return 1.
check_char: mov eax, ecx ; eax = input char not eax ; bitwise complement (all 32 bits) and eax, 0FFh ; keep only the low byte cmp eax, 0B4h ; compare against target jne fail mov eax, 1 ret fail: xor eax, eax ret
What single ASCII character passed in cl makes check_char return 1?
---
Answer: 'K' (0x4B / decimal 75)
1. `not eax` flips every bit of the 32-bit register, so if ecx holds the input byte c, after not the low byte becomes (~c) & 0xFF (upper bits get masked off next anyway). 2. The check requires (~c) & 0xFF == 0xB4. Solve backward: invert the target -- ~0xB4 & 0xFF = 0x4B -- since NOT is its own inverse. 3. 0x4B is ASCII 'K'. Feeding 'K' in cl makes eax land on 0xB4, the jne falls through, and the function returns 1.
